Definition: Rechum, the name of a Persian and of three Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Rehum the chancellor wrote the letter to Artaxerxes against the rebuilding of Jerusalem, another Rehum came up with Zerubbabel from the exile, and a third Rehum repaired the wall of Jerusalem. The letter of the chancellor slowed the work for a season, but the builders named Rehum carried it on.
TheologicalSignificance: I am convinced that the same name can belong to an enemy and to builders, and God tells them apart.
RelatedPeople: Rehum, Chancellor; Rehum, Son of Bani; Ezra; Nehemiah
